analysis.subject: earth-science
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers how temperature pressure and density vary with altitude and defines English units atmosphere model with three zones troposphere lower stratosphere upper stratosphere plus density equation and simulation note

overview.headline: Layered standard atmosphere model linking temperature pressure and density to altitude

keyPoints.point: Atmosphere is extremely thin sheet extending from surface to edge of space about 60 miles
keyPoints.quote: an extremely thin sheet of air extending from the surface of the Earth to the edge of space, about 60 miles above the surface of the Earth.

keyPoints.point: Temperature highest near surface and decreases as altitude increases while pressure also decreases with altitude
keyPoints.quote: Thus the air temperature is highest near the surface and decreases as altitude increases.

keyPoints.point: Troposphere runs from surface to 36,152 feet with temperature decreasing linearly and pressure decreasing exponentially
keyPoints.quote: The troposphere runs from the surface of the Earth to 36,152 feet.

keyPoints.point: Density in each zone derived from equation of state using pressure and temperature
keyPoints.quote: In each zone the density rho (ρ) is derived from the equation of state:

keyTerms.gloss: troposphere is lowest zone from surface to 36,152 feet where temperature falls
keyTerms.quote: The troposphere runs from the surface of the Earth to 36,152 feet.

keyTerms.gloss: rate of temperature decrease with altitude in troposphere
keyTerms.quote: The rate of temperature decrease is called the lapse rate.

keyTerms.gloss: density depends on temperature and pressure through equation of state
keyTerms.quote: The air density depends on both the temperature and the pressure through the equation of state and also decreases with increasing altitude.

keyTerms.gloss: lower stratosphere zone with constant temperature from 36,152 feet to 82,345 feet
keyTerms.quote: The lower stratosphere runs from 36,152 feet to 82,345 feet.

keyTerms.gloss: equation of state relates density pressure and temperature within each zone
keyTerms.quote: In each zone the density rho (ρ) is derived from the equation of state:

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Layered zones build in altitude order so sequence helps learners see where each temperature and pressure curve applies
componentPlan.focusQuote: The model has three zones with separate curve fits for the troposphere, the lower stratosphere, and the upper stratosphere.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Exploring density equation shows how pressure and temperature values generate density for any altitude zone
